anchor_commit.description: Git HEAD recorded automatically when the DAG is created. This is a provenance/drift marker only, not an execution base, repository snapshot, cleanliness requirement, or commit-matching guard. Discovery, reads, preview, compilation, and execution use the live repository state.

satisfied_by.description: Optional ALL-of relationship and the DAG's only edge. When present, every referenced child must be satisfied. Omission denotes an unresolved semantic leaf. References may converge on shared descendants but must never create a path back to an ancestor. If any referenced child is type 'run', every other referenced child must be type 'semantic'.

overwrite.description: When true, atomically replace an existing destination with the moved source (native replace). When false (default), the destination must not already exist and a collision is an ordinary recoverable terminal failure.

command.description: Execution command as an argv array, executed with shell=False. It is not a shell string. One canonical policy module checks it against an exact executable-plus-subcommand allowlist.

exclusive.description: When true, execute this run node without any other run node executing concurrently within the active DAG.

oneOf.description: Terminal command node and satisfaction barrier for implementation/verification work. Its semantic parent may have semantic siblings for it, but no other terminal siblings. Publication lifecycle commands such as commit, push, PR creation, release, or deployment belong outside the Change DAG; a local executor-generated checkpoint commit on successful DAG completion is separate executor lifecycle behavior, not a run node. exclusive defaults to false. command is an argv array executed with shell=False through one canonical policy allowlist.

$comment: The Change DAG validator enforces invariants beyond JSON shape: satisfied_by is the only ALL-of graph edge; root, reachability, acyclicity, shared-descendant identity, derived depth, and run-child constraints are validated; anchor_commit is provenance only; unresolved semantic leaves are valid but unsatisfied.
